newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel says Arafat wants Malta meeting, PLO says no.
newsitem.headline: Israel says Arafat wants Malta meeting, PLO says no.

text.p: Israel said on Monday Palestinian President Yasser Arafat had expressed interest in meeting Foreign Minister David Levy at Europe-Mediterranean talks in Malta to defuse the crisis in Middle East peace talks.
But PLO officials said the Palestinian leader, who was consulting with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak in Cairo on Monday before going to Malta, has ruled out a meeting with Levy at this stage.
Israeli Foreign Ministry director-general Eytan Bentsur said the Palestinian approach was made through European envoy Miguel Angel Moratinos.

"We received a message from Mr Moratinos, the European envoy, about an interest by...Mr Arafat and Mr Abu Mazen to meet with the foreign minister," Bentsur told Israel Radio after a spokesman announced Levy would attend the talks in Malta.
"When the foreign minister arrives in Malta and if the approach is made, I estimate he will take a positive view (of such a meeting)," he said.
Palestinian officials had said Moratinos proposed Arafat meet Levy to defuse a crisis in Israeli-PLO peace talks that began when Israel began a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem last month.
They said the proposal was part of a European initiative to revive talks but the Palestinian Authority wanted Israel to first halt settlement construction.
"There won't be any meeting with Levy during the Malta conference," Arafat aide Nabil Abu Rdainah told Reuters.
Countries attending the two-day conference are to discuss advancing the 27-member EU-Mediterranean Partnership created in Barcelona in 1995.

Israeli commentators said Levy was concerned Arab states would use the forum to criticise Israel for its settlement of occupied land but EU council president Hans van Mierlo said the Arabs have agreed not to raise the issue.
Palestinians view East Jerusalem as the capital of their future state and say the settlement violates international law. Israel claims all of Jerusalem as its capital.

Arafat told reporters at Cairo airport before heading to talks with Mubarak that they would discuss how to protect peace "particularly in light of continued Israeli efforts to break the agreements signed in Washington and Cairo."
